findings.title: BCB VASP Licensing Deadline: October 30, 2026 – Unauthorised Crypto Firms Must Cease Operations
findings.summary: Existing VASPs that were operating in Brazil on or before February 2, 2026 must file BCB authorisation requests by October 30, 2026. After that date, licensed banks and payment institutions may not transact with unauthorised crypto providers, and non-compliant firms must cease operations within 30 days.
findings.client_impact: HNW clients with crypto holdings at Brazilian exchanges risk losing access to banking rails and potentially their assets if their provider has not obtained BCB authorisation by October 30. Advisors should verify the compliance status of any Brazilian VASP used by clients immediately.
findings.urgency_reason: Hard deadline 18 days away (October 30, 2026); post-deadline, banks cut off unauthorised providers and client assets may be inaccessible.
findings.source_name: FCM Law – Brazil VASP Licence: BCB Rules, Deadlines and FAQ (2026)

findings.title: Florida SB 264 Foreign Buyer Restrictions Upheld by Eleventh Circuit; Constitutional Amendment HJR 1-F on November 3, 2026 Ballot
findings.summary: The Eleventh Circuit upheld Florida's SB 264 in November 2025, restricting property acquisitions by individuals and entities linked to China, Russia, Iran, North Korea, Cuba, Venezuela (Maduro government), and Syria, particularly within 10 miles of military or critical infrastructure. Constitutional amendment HJR 1-F, which may further affect foreign ownership rights, appears on the November 3, 2026 Florida ballot.
findings.client_impact: Clients connected to any of the seven designated countries must avoid prohibited Florida real estate acquisitions now that the law is upheld and enforceable; advisors should review any pending or contemplated transactions before November 3 and monitor the ballot outcome, which could expand or entrench these restrictions.
findings.urgency_reason: Constitutional amendment ballot is 22 days away (November 3, 2026); SB 264 is already enforceable, making pre-transaction review urgent for affected clients.
findings.source_name: Cueto Law Group – Florida SB 264 Foreign Ownership Law Explained (2026)

findings.title: JFSC 2027 Thematic Programme: Customer Risk Assessment Questionnaire Launching October 2026
findings.summary: The JFSC set its 2027 thematic examination focus on financial crime compliance. The first phase begins with a customer risk assessment questionnaire being distributed to regulated entities in October 2026, signalling formal examinations will follow in H1 2027.
findings.client_impact: FGC or client entities regulated in Jersey should expect to receive and respond to the JFSC questionnaire this month; weak CRA documentation now will translate directly into examination findings in early 2027.
findings.urgency_reason: Questionnaire distribution begins this month (October 2026); entities should prepare CRA documentation immediately rather than waiting for the formal exam.
findings.source_name: Channel Eye – Financial Services Regulatory Summary: September 2026

findings.title: DIFC Prescribed Companies 2026 Regulations – Open Application and Six-Month Transition
findings.summary: The DIFC Prescribed Companies Regulations 2026 opened establishment to any applicant and standardised compliance requirements including use of a licensed Corporate Service Provider. Existing companies have a six-month transition period from the regulations' effective date to comply.
findings.client_impact: Clients using DIFC Prescribed Companies as wealth holding structures must appoint a licensed CSP and verify compliance with the new framework before the transition deadline, which falls approximately December 2026; non-compliance may affect the validity of the structure.
findings.urgency_reason: Six-month transition from the June 2026 effective date points to a ~December 2026 deadline; clients need to act in the next 4-6 weeks.
findings.source_name: The Legal 500 – DIFC Prescribed Companies: Key Changes Under The 2026 Regulations

findings.title: Luxembourg DAC9 and Pillar Two: First GloBE Information Return Exchanges Due December 31, 2026
findings.summary: Luxembourg's DAC9 Law (adopted December 2025) requires the first GloBE Information Return exchange for fiscal years starting on or after December 31, 2023 to take place by December 31, 2026. Non-compliance carries penalties up to EUR 300,000.
findings.client_impact: MNE clients with Luxembourg holding or operating entities must confirm their GloBE Information Return filings are on track for the December 31, 2026 exchange; advisors should verify that filing agents and group tax functions have the required data prepared.
findings.urgency_reason: Statutory deadline is December 31, 2026 — approximately 80 days out — with significant penalty exposure; preparation should be actively underway now.
findings.source_name: Mondaq / Arendt – Luxembourg: Pillar Two and DAC9 Adoption

findings.title: Panama Law 526 Economic Substance Requirements – Effective from 2027 Fiscal Year
findings.summary: Panama Law 526 (enacted May 28, 2026, implemented by Decree 32 of September 2, 2026) requires Panama entities in multinational groups that earn foreign passive income to demonstrate genuine local economic substance or pay a 15% tax on that income, effective from fiscal years beginning January 1, 2027.
findings.client_impact: Clients with Panama holding entities or passive income vehicles inside multinational groups have roughly 80 days to assess whether their structures meet the substance test and restructure if needed before the 2027 fiscal year begins.
findings.urgency_reason: Compliance window closes January 1, 2027; structures without adequate substance face a 15% tax charge from day one of 2027, so pre-year-end review is time-sensitive.
findings.source_name: ALTA Legal – Panama Law 526 2026: Changes to Income Tax (Economic Substance)

findings.title: Cayman AEOI: CRS Annual Filing Deadline Was July 31, 2026; Principal Point of Contact Appointment Due January 31, 2027
findings.summary: The 2026 CRS XML filing and compliance form deadlines (July 31 and September 2026) have passed. Under amended regulations (SL 50 of 2025), the annual deadline moves to June 30 starting from 2027 filings. Entities without a Cayman principal point of contact must appoint one by January 31, 2027.
findings.client_impact: Cayman funds and entities without a designated principal point of contact must appoint one before January 31, 2027, or face non-compliance with CRS obligations; advisors should also note the earlier June 30 annual deadline that applies from 2027.
findings.urgency_reason: January 31, 2027 PPOC appointment deadline is approximately 111 days away; the earlier annual CRS deadline from 2027 (June 30 vs prior July 31) requires calendar adjustments for the next reporting cycle.
findings.source_name: Maples Group – Cayman AEOI: 2026 Deadlines and Regulatory Updates

findings.title: ADGM FSRA Funds Framework Amendments Take Immediate Effect – Transition Period Until March 31, 2027
findings.summary: ADGM FSRA amendments effective September 16, 2026 update requirements for sub-threshold fund managers, institutional fund managers, employer investment vehicles, and foreign fund managers. Venture Capital Fund Managers and Foreign Fund Managers have a transition period until March 31, 2027.
findings.client_impact: Fund managers and family offices with ADGM authorisations should confirm whether any of the four affected categories apply to them and begin transition planning; the March 31, 2027 deadline is roughly 170 days out but requires regulatory analysis and potentially new documentation.
findings.urgency_reason: Transition period runs to March 31, 2027; early-stage compliance review is advisable given the breadth of affected entity types and the need for regulatory counsel.
findings.source_name: TaxAdepts – ADGM FSRA Finalises Funds Framework Enhancements

findings.title: AIFMD II Transposed April 16, 2026 – Open-Ended AIF Liquidity Tools Grace Period Until April 16, 2027
findings.summary: EU member states were required to transpose AIFMD II by April 16, 2026 (Germany complied with the FRiG). Open-ended AIFs constituted before April 16, 2026 have until April 16, 2027 to implement mandatory liquidity management tools. Loan-originating AIFs face new leverage caps. New Annex IV reporting begins April 16, 2027.
findings.client_impact: Clients invested in or managing open-ended EU AIFs constituted before April 2026 must implement required liquidity management tools by April 16, 2027; fund managers should be actively reviewing their governance documents and redemption procedures now.
findings.urgency_reason: Grace period expires April 16, 2027 — approximately six months away — requiring document drafting, legal review and potentially investor notifications before the deadline.
findings.source_name: Skadden – AIFMD II Roundup: Key Reforms, EU Implementation and the UK Alternative

findings.title: Bahamas CFATF Fifth Round Mutual Evaluation Scheduled for Q4 2026
findings.summary: The Central Bank of The Bahamas confirmed the country will undergo its Fifth Round CFATF Mutual Evaluation in Q4 2026, assessing the effectiveness of its AML/CFT regime. Preliminary findings may drive near-term regulatory guidance.
findings.client_impact: Clients with Bahamas-domiciled entities or banking relationships should monitor for regulatory changes or enhanced due diligence requirements that typically follow or precede a FATF-style evaluation, particularly around UBO disclosure and transaction monitoring.
findings.urgency_reason: Evaluation is underway in Q4 2026 now; post-evaluation recommendations could require rapid compliance adjustments by Bahamas-regulated entities.
findings.source_name: Central Bank of The Bahamas – Q2 2026 Quarterly Regulatory Letter

findings.title: BCB Resolution 561 Restricts Stablecoin Use in Cross-Border Payments – Effective October 1, 2026
findings.summary: BCB Resolution 561 (effective October 1, 2026) closes the payment rail previously used for stablecoin and crypto settlement in cross-border transactions by eFX firms. Companies wishing to continue this activity must apply for BCB approval by May 2027.
findings.client_impact: Brazilian HNW clients or entities using stablecoin rails for international remittances or payments through eFX firms must transition to alternative BCB-compliant payment channels immediately; any pending cross-border payment structures relying on these rails need urgent review.
findings.urgency_reason: Rule is already in force as of October 1, 2026; affected clients need to identify alternative payment mechanisms now, with the BCB approval window running until May 2027 for those wishing to continue.
findings.source_name: CoinDesk – Brazil's Central Bank Bans Stablecoin and Crypto Settlement in Cross-Border Payments

findings.title: IRS Issues Rev. Rul. 2026-20 and Notice 2026-62 Targeting ETF Tax-Aware Fund Strategies
findings.summary: The IRS and Treasury issued Rev. Rul. 2026-20 and Notice 2026-62 in late September / early October 2026 targeting ETF transactions involving transfers of appreciated securities and other tax-aware fund strategies the government considers inconsistent with federal tax rules.
findings.client_impact: HNW clients and family offices holding or considering ETF structures that rely on tax-aware or in-kind creation/redemption strategies should have their advisors review those structures against the new guidance immediately to assess exposure to the IRS position.
findings.urgency_reason: Guidance is already published; existing structures must be reviewed for compliance risk, and new strategies should not be implemented without confirming they fall outside the scope of the ruling and notice.
findings.source_name: KPMG TaxNewsFlash – Week in Tax: September 28 – October 2, 2026

findings.title: Panama Decree 25: FATCA/CRS Controlling-Person Threshold Reduced from 25% to 10%
findings.summary: Panama's Decree 25 reduces the controlling-person threshold for entity accounts from 25% to 10% for FATCA and CRS reporting. It also permits reliance on AML/KYC procedures to identify controlling persons and treats trust settlors and foundation founders as controlling persons.
findings.client_impact: HNW clients who own 10-24% of Panama entities (foundations, corporations, trusts) may now be reportable under CRS/FATCA where they previously were not; advisors should review all Panama entity ownership structures against the new 10% threshold and update KYC files accordingly.
findings.urgency_reason: Decree is already in force (published August 2026); this is an ongoing compliance change requiring review of existing client files and entity ownership maps.
findings.source_name: KPMG TaxNewsFlash – Panama: Ownership Threshold for Controlling Persons Reduced Under FATCA and CRS

findings.title: Cyprus Comprehensive Tax Reform in Force from January 1, 2026 – Fund Redemptions and Withholding Changes
findings.summary: Cyprus's tax reform package (effective January 1, 2026) reclassifies fund redemptions as dividend income potentially subject to Special Defence Contribution, modifies dividend withholding rates, and includes a proposed (unconfirmed) 8% flat tax on crypto gains. AIFMD II implementation is ongoing.
findings.client_impact: Clients with Cyprus-domiciled funds or fund investments should review whether fund redemptions are now triggering SDC exposure and clarify the applicable dividend withholding rate for their investor profile; the potential crypto gains tax warrants monitoring for update.
findings.urgency_reason: Reform is in effect for the full 2026 tax year; without a review, clients may be filing on incorrect assumptions about how their fund redemptions and dividends are taxed.
findings.source_name: Sovereign Group – Cyprus Tax Reform 2026: Corporate and Personal Tax Changes

findings.title: BCB Expands Foreign Currency Account Access – Rules in Force October 1, 2026
findings.summary: The BCB expanded access to foreign currency accounts for Brazilian residents and entities effective October 1, 2026. Accounts prohibit cash withdrawals/deposits and require origin-of-funds documentation. Domestic use of foreign currency for payments within Brazil remains restricted.
findings.client_impact: Brazilian HNW clients may now open BCB-regulated foreign currency accounts to hold international balances, which could simplify cross-border asset management; FGC should brief Brazilian clients on the new account structure and its restrictions.
findings.urgency_reason: Already in force — informational update for Brazilian clients to incorporate into their FX and cash management strategy.
findings.source_name: Banco Central do Brasil – Press Release on FX Account Expansion

findings.title: CVM Resolution 247 Amends Credit Information System Rules for Securitisation Entities and FIDCs
findings.summary: CVM Resolution 247 (October 5, 2026) amends how securitisation firms and FIDCs (Fundos de Investimento em Direitos Creditórios) submit and access data in the BCB's Credit Information System (SCR), aiming to improve data quality and reporting consistency.
findings.client_impact: Clients with interests in Brazilian FIDCs or securitisation vehicles should confirm that their fund administrators have updated SCR reporting procedures in line with Resolution 247; this is primarily an operational compliance update with no immediate investment impact.
findings.urgency_reason: Operational reporting change with no client-facing deadline; included as background awareness for those with FIDC exposure.
findings.source_name: Generation Impact – CVM Resolution 247 on Credit Information System SCR Rules

findings.title: FinCEN Final Rule Permanently Exempts US-Formed Entities from BOI Reporting – Effective August 14, 2026
findings.summary: FinCEN's final rule (effective August 14, 2026) permanently redefines 'reporting company' to cover only foreign entities registered in the US. All US-formed corporations, LLCs, and limited partnerships are now permanently exempt from BOI filing. FinCEN will delete previously reported information from US persons. The 2016 CDD Rule for financial institutions remains in force.
findings.client_impact: US-formed holding companies, LLCs, and limited partnerships used by HNW clients are permanently relieved of CTA BOI filing obligations — a significant reduction in compliance burden; clients who previously filed may have their information deleted from the FinCEN database.
findings.urgency_reason: Beneficial change already in force since August 14, 2026; no action needed beyond advising clients of the relief and confirming their structures qualify as US-formed entities.
findings.source_name: Harvard Law School Forum on Corporate Governance – FinCEN Permanently Eliminates BOI Reporting Requirements

findings.title: BVI Beneficial Ownership Register: Full Enforcement Since March 31, 2026; Legitimate Interest Access Since April 1, 2026
findings.summary: The BVI FSC's grace period ended March 31, 2026; all BVI entities must have identified and reported beneficial owners in VIRRGIN. From April 1, 2026, qualifying persons may apply for access to limited BO information on individuals with 25%+ ownership. The register remains non-public.
findings.client_impact: All BVI entities used by FGC clients should by now have filed BO information in VIRRGIN; any entity that missed the March 31 deadline is exposed to a restriction notice and should remediate immediately.
findings.urgency_reason: Enforcement is already active — raised as a compliance verification reminder for any BVI entity in the client portfolio that has not yet confirmed its VIRRGIN filing.
findings.source_name: Trident Trust – Access to BVI Register of Beneficial Ownership

findings.title: Luxembourg Carried Interest Reform in Force for 2026 Tax Year
findings.summary: Luxembourg enacted carried interest tax reform (Bill 8590) applicable from the 2026 tax year, targeting investment fund carried interest received by qualifying fund managers and providing greater tax certainty and competitive treatment.
findings.client_impact: Fund managers with Luxembourg-domiciled vehicles may benefit from improved and more predictable tax treatment of carried interest starting with the 2026 tax year; local fund counsel and tax advisors should review eligibility and update LP agreement provisions if needed.
findings.urgency_reason: In force for 2026 — no immediate deadline, but relevant for any client who manages or receives carried interest from Luxembourg funds.
findings.source_name: Lexology – Luxembourg Tax Update: What's New in 2026

findings.title: FINMA Opens Consultation on Revised Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance – Consultation Closed June 2026
findings.summary: FINMA's consultation on a partial revision of its AMLO-FINMA (to address FATF criticism ahead of Switzerland's 2027 mutual evaluation) closed June 9, 2026. Final rules are expected to tighten CDD requirements and documentation standards for regulated wealth managers.
findings.client_impact: Swiss-regulated wealth managers and portfolio managers should anticipate enhanced CDD requirements when the revised ordinance is finalised; a gap analysis of current KYC procedures against anticipated FATF standards is advisable in preparation.
findings.urgency_reason: Consultation closed; final rules forthcoming — no immediate deadline but preparation ahead of the 2027 FATF evaluation will reduce compliance disruption when rules are published.
findings.source_name: Fincrime Central – Swiss Regulator FINMA Updates Anti-Money Laundering Standards for 2026

findings.title: FINMA Guidance 01/2026: Crypto-Based Asset Custody Requirements for Portfolio Managers
findings.summary: FINMA Guidance 01/2026 (January 12, 2026) requires crypto assets in individual portfolio management to be held with prudentially supervised custodians that provide client asset segregation and bankruptcy protection.
findings.client_impact: Portfolio managers holding digital assets for Swiss-regulated clients must confirm their custodian arrangements meet FINMA's segregation and supervision standards; any custodian that is not prudentially supervised must be replaced.
findings.urgency_reason: Guidance published January 2026 — ongoing compliance obligation; raised as a reminder for any client or manager holding crypto through a Swiss portfolio mandate.
findings.source_name: Borel Barbey – FINMA Guidance 01/2026 on Custody of Crypto-Based Assets

findings.title: MAS Asset Management Hub Package: Tax Exemption for Fund Management Profits (YA2027) and New Passes
findings.summary: MAS and MOF announced (August 19, 2026) a new tax exemption for qualifying fund management profits from YA2027, a Hedge Fund Investment Programme, and an Investment Management Track under the ONE Pass for senior fund professionals. Single family offices also benefit from a revised class exemption effective June 15, 2026.
findings.client_impact: HNW families considering Singapore as a base for their family office or fund management activities will benefit from a more competitive tax environment from 2027; the revised SFO class exemption already in force may also simplify Singapore structures for qualifying clients.
findings.urgency_reason: Positive development with no action deadline; relevant for clients evaluating Singapore domiciliation or expansion of existing Singapore structures.
findings.source_name: MAS Media Release – MAS Introduces Measures to Strengthen Singapore's Competitiveness as a Leading Asset Management Hub

findings.title: MAS Source of Wealth Circular AMLD 05/2026 – Risk-Proportionate Approach to SOW Checks
findings.summary: MAS Circular AMLD 05/2026 (May 25, 2026) guides financial institutions on conducting source-of-wealth checks in a risk-proportionate manner, aiming to reduce excessive documentation burdens while maintaining mandatory SOW requirements and enabling faster onboarding.
findings.client_impact: HNW clients onboarding with Singapore financial institutions should experience faster account opening where wealth sources are well-documented; advisors should brief clients on the right level of documentation to satisfy the risk-proportionate standard.
findings.urgency_reason: Circular already in force — beneficial change for client onboarding; no action deadline.
findings.source_name: Alpadis – MAS Guidance on Source of Wealth: What Risk-Proportionate Asks of Financial Institutions

findings.title: ADGM Registration Authority Publishes 2026-2027 Regulatory Priorities – October 1, 2026
findings.summary: The ADGM Registration Authority published ten priority areas for 2026-2027 including annual filings, licence renewals, beneficial ownership compliance, and audit quality, signalling areas of heightened supervisory focus.
findings.client_impact: ADGM-registered entities should review their compliance programmes against the stated priorities, particularly beneficial ownership disclosure and financial statement quality, to reduce the likelihood of regulatory escalation.
findings.urgency_reason: Forward-looking supervisory signal — no immediate deadline, but useful context for clients planning ADGM compliance reviews.
findings.source_name: TaxAdepts – ADGM Regulatory Priorities 2026-2027: What Changes

findings.title: SBP Acuerdo 01-2026 Tightens AML/CFT Documentation for Banks and Financial Institutions
findings.summary: SBP Acuerdo 01-2026 (effective January 2026) tightens AML/CFT documentation requirements at account opening and during ongoing monitoring for all entities under SBP supervision, increasing verification obligations for new and existing clients.
findings.client_impact: Panama-based banking relationships for HNW clients may face enhanced documentation requests at periodic review; clients should keep source-of-wealth and beneficial ownership documentation current with their Panama banking institutions.
findings.urgency_reason: Already in force since January 2026 — background awareness item; clients with Panama banking relationships should confirm existing KYC files are up to date.
findings.source_name: Global Law Experts – Panama Fintech Law 2026: Draft Law No. 314 & SBP Rule 1-2026

findings.title: MFSA New Credit Institution Regulations and Conduct Rulebook Effective October 6, 2026
findings.summary: The MFSA published new regulations for credit and financial institutions plus a Conduct of Business Rulebook for credit institutions offering retail products, effective October 6, 2026, implementing EU Banking Package provisions (CRD VI / CRR III).
findings.client_impact: Clients with Malta banking or financial institution relationships should verify that their Malta counterparts have updated their compliance frameworks under the new rulebook, which may affect product terms, reporting requirements, or conduct standards.
findings.urgency_reason: In force as of October 6, 2026 — informational for clients with Malta banking or credit institution exposure.
findings.source_name: MFSA – New Regulations for Credit Institutions and Financial Institutions Applicable from 6 October 2026

findings.title: Bahamas Nominee Director Ban Transition Closed July 19, 2026; DAOs Act 2026 Enacted
findings.summary: The Bahamas nominee director prohibition took full effect July 19, 2026; all Bahamas entities must have disclosed actual directors. The Decentralised Autonomous Organisations (DAOs) Act, 2026 and Usufruct Interest Act, 2026 were also enacted during 2026.
findings.client_impact: Any Bahamas entity still using nominee directors is non-compliant as of July 19, 2026 and requires immediate remediation; the DAOs Act is relevant for clients exploring DAO-based ownership or governance structures.
findings.urgency_reason: Compliance deadline passed July 2026 — any non-compliant entity needs urgent remediation; included as a verification reminder.
findings.source_name: Bahamas Financial Services Board – Acts, Amendments & Regulations (2026)

findings.title: Guernsey GFSC Stablecoin Rules Forthcoming Autumn 2026; MONEYVAL Consultation Closed October 9
findings.summary: The GFSC will publish feedback and new stablecoin rules in Autumn 2026. Its MONEYVAL-responsive AML/CFT consultation closed October 9, 2026. Regulated entities should monitor the GFSC website for both sets of guidance.
findings.client_impact: Guernsey-regulated fund managers or clients holding stablecoin assets in Guernsey structures should monitor for the forthcoming GFSC stablecoin rules, which may impose new custody or disclosure requirements.
findings.urgency_reason: Rules forthcoming but not yet published — no current client action, monitor for release.
findings.source_name: Mourant – Guernsey FinReg Quarterly Update Q3 2026

findings.title: Isle of Man Embeds OECD Pillar Two Side-by-Side Package in Domestic Law
findings.summary: Isle of Man legislation incorporates the OECD's January 2026 Side-by-Side Package as an updated source of Administrative Guidance for Pillar Two, including new safe harbours for low-risk situations, keeping IoM rules aligned with the latest OECD framework.
findings.client_impact: MNE clients with Isle of Man holding or operating entities should confirm with their IoM advisors whether any of the new Pillar Two safe harbours apply to their structures and whether they reduce ongoing compliance obligations.
findings.urgency_reason: Alignment update with no immediate deadline — background awareness for clients with IoM entities in Pillar Two scope.
findings.source_name: OECD Pillars – Pillar Two Developments Tracker 2026

findings.title: OECD Pillar Two Side-by-Side Package: New Safe Harbours Agreed January 2026
findings.summary: The OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework agreed on the Pillar Two Side-by-Side package in January 2026, introducing a Simplified ETR Safe Harbour, a one-year extension of the Transitional CbCR Safe Harbour, a Substance-based Tax Incentive Safe Harbour, and two additional safe harbours. May 2026 updates added late-filing penalty guidance and UTPR safe harbour refinements.
findings.client_impact: MNE clients subject to Pillar Two should have their tax advisors assess eligibility for the new safe harbours, particularly the Simplified ETR and Substance-based Incentive safe harbours, which could materially reduce compliance and top-up tax costs.
findings.urgency_reason: Safe harbours are agreed and available — no deadline, but failing to claim eligible safe harbours creates unnecessary compliance cost.
findings.source_name: KPMG – OECD: Agreement Reached on Pillar Two Side-by-Side Package
